bennum: a sickness, UNCERTAIN: bennī (bi-en-ni), the name of an illness that strikes a slave after sale (Harper’s glossary: “a kind of fever”); the nature of the illness and the ending -ī (not the nominative) are not understood, so the word is kept as a name, “the bennu-sickness”
baqrum: claim (Harper’s glossary BAKRU “claim”, from baqārum “to make a claim”): baqrī (ba-aq-ri, plural, oblique case) “claims”: baqrī irtaši “claims have arisen (?)”, baqrī ippal “he shall answer the claims”; the AK sign is read aq (Harper prints ag in the text)
nukurtum: enmity, hostility (Harper’s glossary “enmity”): nukurtim (nu-ku-ur-tim, genitive) in ina māt nukurtim “in a hostile country”, i.e. an enemy land
šunu: they (the independent 3rd-person plural masculine pronoun, nominative): šunu (šu-nu) “they (are)”, making a nominal sentence with no verb: šumma wardum u amtum šunu mārū mātim “if the male slave and the female slave are natives”
pâqum: to take into one’s care, to be entrusted with (Harper’s glossary, PAKU, from a verb he writes paku), UNCERTAIN: ipaq (i-pa-aq, the last sign AK read aq) “he shall take back (?)”, the sense “take back into his own care” being a guess from the context

__broaden__.maqātum: to fall, collapse: imqutma (im-ku-ut-ma, preterite + -ma) “it has fallen, and” · imqutu (im-ku-tu, imqut with the subjunctive -u) “(which) fell”, “and it fell”: bītam imqutu “the house that fell” · verb · imtaqut (im-ta-ku-ut, written with the KU sign, which stands for qu) perfect “has fallen”, said of a sickness that has fallen on a man: bennī elīšu imtaqut “the bennu-sickness has fallen on him”
__broaden__.nādinānum: seller: nādin “the seller (who)” · nādinānšu (na-di-na-an-šu) “his seller”, nādinānišu (na-di-na-ni-šu, genitive + -šu) “his seller”: ana nādinānišu “to his seller” · nādinānum “seller” is the opposite of šayyāmānum “buyer”
__broaden__.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver” · kasap (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) construct “silver of”: kasap tirḫatim “silver of the bride-price” · kaspi (KÙ.BABBAR, no complement written; Harper’s normalization) in kaspi mišil šīmišu “silver, half its price” · kaspam (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) “the silver” as object: kaspam išqulu “the silver he weighed out” · kaspima (KÙ.BABBAR-ma) kaspi + -ma, genitive after balum: balum kaspima “without any silver”
__broaden__.apālum: to answer; to satisfy, pay (a creditor): ippalma (present, with -ma) “he shall pay, and” · uppal (u-up-pa-al) “she shall pay”, taken as a present (a G present would be ippal; the u- is unexplained), in šaniam ul uppal, UNCERTAIN · apālam (a-pa-lam, infinitive, accusative) “to pay”: apālam lā ileʾʾi “he is not able to pay” · ippal (i-ip-pa-al, present) “he shall answer, meet (a claim)”: nādinānšu baqrī ippal “his seller shall answer the claims”
__broaden__.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share” · libbaša, libbiša (li-ib-ba-ša, li-ib-bi-ša) “her heart”: mala libbiša “as much as her heart wants”; libbaša uṭabbū “they shall make her heart good”, i.e. content her · ša libbiša (li-ib-bi-ša) “what is in her womb”, literally “that of her heart”, the unborn child: ana ša libbiša “for what was in her womb” · libbu (li-ib-bu) in ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land” (Harper’s form; after ina one would expect libbi)
__broaden__.mātum: land, country · māt (ma-at) the form before a following genitive, “the land of”: ina māt nukurtim “in a hostile country” · mātim (ma-tim, or the Sumerogram KALAM, no ending written) genitive “of the land”: ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land”, mārū mātim “natives of the country”, mātim šanītim “another country”
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate” · ittalkamma (it-ta-al-kam-ma) perfect ittalkam (ittalak + the ventive -am, “hither”) “he has come”, + -ma “and”
__broaden__.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading) · bēlišu (be-li-šu) “its owner” (of an animal), bēlišuma “to its owner only” (with the emphatic -ma); bēl alpim “the owner of the ox” · bēl epinnim “the owner of the plough”, bēl tarbaṣim “the owner of the pen”; bēlīšunu (be-li-šu-nu) “their owners”, the owners of the cattle and sheep a herdsman has lost · bēl (be-el) “owner of” before a genitive: bēl wardim “the owner of the male slave” · bēlī (be-li) “my master”: ul bēlī atta “you are not my master” · bēlšu, bēlišu (be-el-šu, be-li-šu) “his master”
__broaden__.edûm-D: UNCERTAIN verb, read as the D-stem of edûm “to know”: “to make known, to identify, to point out”: uwaddīma (u-wi-id-di-ma) “he has identified (?), and”, D-stem + -ma; the form and the sense are UNCERTAIN · D-stem verb · utēddi (u-te-id-di) “he has identified (?)”, read as the D-stem perfect of edûm (Harper’s glossary lists it under edû, II,2); the form and the sense are UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son” · mārī (DUMU-i) “my son” (-ī “my”); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “children” in mārī ūlissum “children she bore him”; mārū (DUMU{meš}) “sons” as subject: mārū ana ummātim ul izuzzū “the sons shall not divide by mothers” · mār X (DUMU, the sign TUR) “a member of the class X”, literally “son of X”: mār ummiānim “a craftsman”, mār zinništim “the son of a woman”; māram (DUMU) “a son”, mārašu (DUMU-šu) “his son”, mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons”, mārīšu “his sons” · mārū (DUMU{meš}, plural, nominative) “sons”: mārū mātim “sons of the land”, i.e. natives, as a predicate
__broaden__.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan · išakkanūši “they shall set (her on a stake)”, išakkanūšumma “they shall set (it) aside for him, and” · idiom panam šakānum (panam ištakan) “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind · iššakkan also written iš-ta-ak-ka-an (Harper’s reading, UNCERTAIN): andurār amtim iššakkan “the release of the slave-woman shall be established” · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be set”: andurāršunu iššakkan “their release shall be set”
__broaden__.šanûm: another, a second one: ana šanîm “to another”, šanûm “another man” · feminine šanītum “another (woman)”: šanītam, šanītim (ša-ni-tam, ša-ni-tim), in the accusative and genitive · šaniam (ša-ni-a-am, accusative) “another”: šaniam ul uppal “nor shall she pay another (?)”, UNCERTAIN · šanītim (ša-ni-tim) feminine genitive “another”, agreeing with mātim: mātim šanītim “another country”
__broaden__.qabûm: to speak, say: iqbû, iqtabi, iqabbûma · iqabbi (written i-qa₂-ab-bi-ma, iqabbi + -ma; Harper prints the GA sign as ga, read qa₂) present “he shall say, declare”: ina maḫar ilim … iqabbima “he shall declare before the god”
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; __broaden__.kânum-D: D-stem of kânum: to convict, prove against someone (uktīn, ukannūšuma) · uktīn (uk-ti-in, perfect, with the infixed -t-) “he has convicted”; ukannūšuma (u-ka-an-nu-šu-ma, present, plural, with -šu “him” and -ma) “they shall convict him, and”; ukānma (u-ka-an-ma, present, singular) “he shall convict, and” · ukannūšima (u-ka-an-nu-ši-ma) “they shall convict her, and”, present plural with -ši “her” and -ma · ukān (u-ka-an) present “he shall prove, convict”: ukānšuma (u-ka-an-šu-ma, with -šu “him” and -ma) “he shall convict him, and”
__broaden__.nakāsum: to cut, cut down: ikkis (preterite) “he cut down” · inakkisū (i-na-ak-ki-su) “they shall cut off”, present plural (the ending -sū is written with the one sign su, as Harper prints it): lišānšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his tongue”, tulêša inakkisū “they shall cut off her breast” · inakkisū “they shall cut off”, of the hand(s) and the ear: rittēšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his hand(s)”, uznašu inakkisū “they shall cut off his ear” · ittakis (it-ta-ki-is, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has cut (off)” · inakkis (i-na-ak-ki-is, present, singular) “he shall cut off”: uznašu inakkis “he shall cut off his ear”
